Event and Boss Map Runs

Runs ahead

Season 14 · Maps · Erazure's loot filter

A character that teleports can run rare T1-T3 maps without clearing them: scout the whole map for its map event, do the event, kill the map boss and open the next map. This page compares those runs with full clears, an hour of each, at your own times: type them in or drag the sliders. Each slider is green where the runs come out ahead and red where full clears do, with every other time as it is. Tick Skip on an event you'd rather not do: when it shows, you head for the boss. The fields start at Erazure's estimates. And when you get a unique map whose bosses drop extra uniques, rush them: Unique maps: rush the bosses works out what a rush is worth for your grail.

A run, step by step

  1. Open a rare map rolled the way you like it. Rolling for low monster density only buys a safer scout: the events and the boss don't depend on it.
  2. Teleport over the whole map. Map events spawn as the rooms around you fill with monsters, not as monsters die, so a scout finds an event as surely as a full clear does.
  3. Do the event when its message shows, unless you skip it. The Dark Wanderer, the Treasure Fallen and the Corrupted Heroes always bring all three, so stop scouting after the third.
  4. Kill the map boss, which you'll have passed on the scout, and open the next map.
  • When events show: the Spire of Darkness within the first few teleports; the Dark Wanderer, the Treasure Fallen and the Corrupted Heroes from about a quarter of the way in; the Bitter Depths, Horazon, the Shadow of Mendeln, Gheed and the Altar of the Catalyst about halfway through the scout.
  • What decides it: your time a map besides the scout (making the game, opening the map, town) and how long your full clears take. The calculator below shows where the runs pull ahead at your times.
  • Keep Catalyst Shards from the Altar for later maps: each forces an event on one.
  • Unique maps: the bosses of City of Ureh, Warlord of Blood, Na-Krul's Abyss and Djinn's Domain drop extra uniques, or a treasure explosion, every kill. Rush them and leave: Unique maps: rush the bosses.
  • For the grail, put in your missing items under Your grail (it can take your Grail Planner ticks), and the Corrupted Ear you use: an ear works on every monster of a full clear, but on a run only on the map boss.

      Unique maps: rush the bosses

      The bosses of four unique maps drop extra loot every kill, on top of their own: three of them random uniques, Djinn's Domain's two a treasure explosion of 60 items each. So when you get one of these maps, rush its bosses and leave: for the grail no other map comes close. Unique maps open only in Hell, one a game. Put your time for a rush in each row: from entering the map, teleporting to the bosses and killing them (City of Ureh's: clearing Gregus Mazi's room and killing Zayl the Merciful; Warlord of Blood's: Cory the Imp and Onion the Accused too). The overhead above (making the game, town and stash) comes on top; a unique map needs no rolling. The numbers count your missing items when Your grail has a list, and follow the magic find you picked.

        What stays fixed

        • What drops doesn't change with the times, so a time only changes the hours. The drops come from a model of how the game spawns map events and rolls drops: each of the 29 T1-T3 maps played as often, runs on rare maps rolled to low density with no purple line, full clears on rare maps as a clearer keeps them (one corruption), magic find as set plus the map's own.
        • An event rolls on 34% of rare maps, each of the 9 kinds as often. You always find it: the Dark Wanderer, Treasure Fallen and Corrupted Heroes bring all three, and a Bitter Depths map always has its portal. About 1 map in 12 is an event forced by a Catalyst Shard from the Altar.
        • The Bitter Depths: its 20 Lucion chests (3 items from the lesser chest loot and 2 from the better, opened at character level 95 with your magic find and the map's), Zoltun Kulle's own drop and his treasure explosion (60 items of a T3 map boss's loot, with no magic find), and the area's monsters with its 5 elite packs. Its 7 plain chests are left out (about 3% of the event).
        • A skipped event: when it shows (a three-spawn kind at its first spawn, the Spire at its obelisk), you head straight for the boss, since a map has one event and nothing is left to find. You lose its drops and save its time and the rest of the scout. Skipping the Altar also means no Catalyst Shards, so no forced events. Full clears still do every event: a full clear's time includes them.
        • "Worth doing below" compares a run doing the event with one skipping it, by what you compare, with your other times as they are; with your own maps it also counts the maps the event drops (Horazon's six, Treasure Fallen's) and the full clears they save.
        • Teleports per map come from scouting every layout of every map: the fastest route that fills every room an event can spawn in averages 110, a scout that brings every walkable spot on screen 276. A count between them mixes the two; one outside scales the nearer one.
        • A full clear's time includes the event when the map has one, and every full clear kills the boss. Trade value counts each unique and set item at its median asking price on the trade site (softcore ladder, 30 October) and the currency at its median ask (4 November, a stack's price split over its items): runes, Worldstone Shards at 1, Pandemonium keys, Splinters, Corrupted Ears, crafting infusions, essences, scarabs, sigils, unique maps, perfect gems. Catalyst Shards don't count: the model spends each one on a forced event. Asks, not sales.
        • Gold counts Anya's Zakarum and Horadrim Orbs for rolling (2.7 rolls a map for the runs, 1.7 for full clears) and Gheed's offers; the runes, perfect gems and jewels the rolls also eat are left out.

        How map events spawn

        A map rolls its event once, when it is opened: 11% of non-magical, 17% of magic and 34% of rare T1-T3 maps, one of nine kinds at equal odds. Nothing of it exists until it spawns. A room fills with monsters the first time you come near it: standing in one room fills it and the 8 rooms around it, about 24 tiles across, and a teleport fills the block around where you land. Each newly filled room may bring the event, more likely the more of the map's rooms are filled already; the event then stands in that room or one beside it, and its message shows.

        EventWhen a newly filled room brings itSpawns
        The Bitter Depths, Horazon, the Shadow of Mendeln, Gheed, the Altar of the CatalystNever before about 42% of the map's rooms are filled, then ever more often: usually about halfway through a scout1
        The Dark Wanderer, the Treasure Fallen, the Corrupted Heroes (a portal)The first once a quarter of the rooms are filled, the second past half, the third past three quarters, each 1 room in 43
        The Spire of DarknessAfter 15 rooms, 1 room in 5. Once you use its obelisk, half the new rooms bring a group of shadows, until 6 keys or nine tenths of the rooms1

        How many rooms count as the whole map is set per map, from the Lost Temple's few to the Halls of Torture's many, and the empty blocks at a map's edges count too. A spawn needs open ground near the room's centre, about 2.4 tiles across, so the crowded corners of a map take none. Scouting every room is what makes the late kinds show: a scout that skips parts of the map can miss them.
